title: Agent Pulse
description: One daily evidence-backed decision brief from the coding-agent projects monitored by The Git Reporter.

scope.coverageStatement: V0.2 reports one dated decision brief from direct public source evidence and keeps git motion as a secondary measurement layer. Community feedback metrics are absent until a reproducible feedback collector ships.

inputs.dailyInsight: reported, date-owned Agent Pulse decision brief

editorialRead.headline: Morning Read — August 26, 2026
editorialRead.readHeadline: openclaw/openclaw is the first source to inspect.
editorialRead.oneLineSummary: openclaw/openclaw leads a 3-item attention queue backed by direct receipts; 29 watchlist sources are fresh, 0 need source-health attention, and movement still requires editorial judgment.
editorialRead.dek: Agent Pulse filtered 29 included projects down to 3 items worth finite newsroom attention. The queue protects attention; it does not declare winners.
bullets: openclaw/openclaw — 250 commits today and 1 same-day mapped article, 86.3 below its current daily pace, with 264 hardening-subject points. Inspect the receipt before assigning a story.
NousResearch/hermes-agent — 53 commits landed today. Keep it on watch, but require the next receipt to prove a reader consequence before promoting it.
Kilo-Org/kilocode — No same-day commit after 366 commits in the seven-day window. The pause is notable enough to preserve, not enough to turn into a story.
editorialRead.watchNext: The next meaningful upgrade is feedback flow: issues opened and closed, review latency, stale backlog, and the share of work that starts outside the maintainer team.
editorialRead.caveat: Source-code motion and article coverage are collected. GitHub issue flow, PR review timing, community discussion, and private backlog signals are not.

dailyInsight.headline: Audit terminal-input policy separately from terminal visibility
dailyInsight.insight: If you evaluate an OpenClaw main-branch build containing its shared-terminal input change, audit the terminal-input path as a distinct authority: seeing or managing an operator-opened session should not by itself let an agent send a command into it.
dailyInsight.mechanism: The fresh public OpenClaw change removes agent-side terminal creation, derives input authority from the exact session execution policy, blocks deny mode, requires a one-shot approval for each non-full input, and checks the live delegated run and terminal again immediately before the PTY write.
dailyInsight.whyItMatters: A terminal is an execution boundary, while a shared terminal view is a collaboration feature. Keeping those decisions separate makes an operator’s trust choice inspectable, but the receipts are public implementation and tests rather than proof of any particular release or deployment configuration.

actions.audience: Operator or security owner evaluating an OpenClaw build with shared terminal access
actions.label: Trace one harmless input from policy to terminal
actions.instruction: In a disposable session and terminal, confirm which policy applies to agent input. Verify that deny blocks it, guarded or workspace access presents a separate one-shot review for each harmless command, and the request cannot complete after the agent run or terminal session has ended.

receipts.title: Enforce session permissions for shared terminal input
receipts.supports: Shows the public implementation that binds terminal input to an exact session policy, one-shot approval path, live run authority, and the current terminal manager.

receipts.title: Terminal input policy and authority tests
receipts.supports: Shows the tested behavior for denied and full policies, separate guarded approvals, unavailable review routes, and lost run, session, or Gateway authority.

confidence.basis: The merged public commit, its terminal-tool implementation, its changed protocol language, and focused behavior tests agree on the intended input boundary. The action remains an audit because the evidence does not establish release availability, defaults, or deployment-wide behavior.

dailyInsight.limitation: These main-branch receipts do not establish that a release contains the change, that it is enabled by default, or that every gateway, terminal client, extension, and policy migration shares the same behavior.
dailyInsight.falsifier: Revise or withdraw this call if public release guidance or regression evidence shows that an agent can create a shell, send guarded input without a fresh exact approval, retain authority after its run ends, or write through a replaced terminal manager.
dailyInsight.watchNext: Watch for public release notes and configuration guidance that state how session permission modes, review delivery, and shared terminal ownership behave in supported upgrades.
